claims.text: The starting material is a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix without added Mo or self-lubricating composite phases.
The proposed modification combines Mo doping with incorporation of a Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite phase by spark plasma sintering.
The modification will produce lubricious interfacial phases during sliding.
The lubricious interfacial phases will stabilize the coefficient of friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
The lubricious interfacial phases will reduce wear from room temperature to 800 °C.
Mo-based oxides and MoS2 tribofilms will form during sliding.
Mo-based oxides and MoS2 tribofilms will maintain a protective tribolayer as temperature increases.
At lower temperatures, Mo increases the mechanical strength of the alloy.
At lower temperatures, Mo promotes nucleation of self-lubricating phases.
At elevated temperatures, Mo oxidation and MoS2 produce stable, low-shear tribofilms.
The proposed low-shear tribofilms lower friction.
Relative to baseline CoCrFeNi, the modified composite will have a consistently lower coefficient of friction throughout the tested temperature range.
Relative to baseline CoCrFeNi, the modified composite will have a lower wear rate throughout the tested temperature range.
The expected improvement applies from room temperature to 800 °C under moderate-to-high sliding loads in a controlled atmosphere.
Performance in highly reducing or unusually oxidizing environments is outside the established boundary and requires separate evaluation.
